title: Not all coins are the same
hook: A friend says: "There are thousands of cryptocurrencies. They're all basically bitcoin, right?"
card1: Bitcoin was the first [[cryptocurrency]]. Since then, thousands of others have appeared. Some run their own [[blockchain]]; others are [[token|tokens]] built on top of an existing one.
analogy1: Coins and tokens are like a country's money and gift cards. The money works everywhere in the country. A gift card uses the same system, but it's only as good as the shop that made it.
card2: A [[stablecoin]] tries to always be worth the same as normal money, for example 1 euro or 1 dollar. It is only as safe as the company or the rules that keep it stable.
card3: Meme coins are made for fun or hype, often in minutes. Most have no use at all, and their price depends only on how much attention they get.

newcoin.prompt: A classmate shows you a brand-new token called "SchoolCoin" and says it's "just like bitcoin, but early".

buy.label: Buy 10 practice coins' worth right away
buy.before: You will swap 10 practice coins for SchoolCoin.
buy.what: The next day the creator sold everything. SchoolCoin is now worth nothing, and your 10 practice coins are gone.
buy.why: Anyone can make a new token in minutes. "Just like bitcoin" is a slogan, not a fact.
buy.how: Creating a token on an existing blockchain takes a few clicks. That's why there are thousands of them.
buy.realLife: Being early only matters if the coin is real. Most new tokens fail.

compare.label: Ask how it is different from bitcoin
compare.before: You will ask what makes SchoolCoin special.
compare.what: They can't explain it, only that it "will go up". You haven't lost anything.
compare.why: A coin needs a reason to exist. If no one can say what it's for, the only reason is hype.
compare.how: Bitcoin has its own network, kept running by thousands of computers. A new token often has one creator who controls a lot of it.
compare.realLife: If every answer is about the price, be careful.

research.label: Check who made it, what it's for and who uses it
research.before: You will look up the token before deciding.
research.what: You found it was made yesterday by one anonymous account that owns most of it. You skipped it and kept your coins.
research.why: A few minutes of checking showed the warning signs that the hype hid.
research.how: Block explorers show when a token was created and how many wallets hold it.
research.realLife: Before trusting a new coin, ask: who made it, what is it for, and who uses it?

q1.a: A coin that tries to stay worth the same as normal money
q1.b: A coin that can never lose value
q1.explanation: A stablecoin tries to stay at, say, 1 euro or 1 dollar. It is only as safe as whoever keeps it stable.

q2.prompt: A brand-new token is "just like bitcoin, but early". What is true?
q2.a: Being early means you will get rich
q2.b: Anyone can create a token in minutes, so check it first
q2.c: A token on a big blockchain is as safe as bitcoin
q2.explanation: Making a token is easy and cheap. Most new tokens fail, so check who made it and why.

q3.prompt: What decides a meme coin's price?
q3.a: What it can be used for
q3.explanation: Most meme coins have no use. Their price rises and falls with attention.

misc.stableIsSafe: "Stable means it can never fail." A stablecoin is only as safe as whoever keeps it stable. Some have collapsed.
misc.stableIsBitcoin: "A stablecoin is bitcoin." Bitcoin's price moves a lot. Stablecoins try not to move.
misc.earlyRich: "Being early means getting rich." Early only pays off if the coin is real. Most new tokens end up worthless.
misc.sameAsBitcoin: "Built on a big blockchain means safe." The blockchain may be safe; the token on top can still be worthless.
misc.memeValue: "Meme coins have a use." Most have none. The price is only attention.
misc.memeGuaranteed: "The creator guarantees the price." No one can guarantee a price.

t1: There are thousands of coins and [[token|tokens]]. Most are nothing like bitcoin.
t2: A [[stablecoin]] tries to stay at 1 euro or 1 dollar, but it is only as safe as whoever keeps it stable.
t3: Before you trust a new coin, ask who made it, what it's for and who uses it.
talk1: Why do you think so many new coins are created every day?
talk2: Which gift cards or loyalty points do we use at home? How are they like tokens?
